title: Sagecrest Medical - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Maya to share onboarding deck, SSO/SAML guide, and draft runbook by 2027-02-16
Daniel to provision benchmark test plan and confirm dataset access points by 2027-02-18
Priya to schedule weekly implementation syncs starting 2027-02-22
action_items: Maya Chen: Send onboarding deck + SSO docs - due 2027-02-16
Daniel Park: Share benchmark plan and sample inference tests - due 2027-02-18
Tasha Bell: Provide sample PII-scrubbed dataset and network contacts for VPC peering - due 2027-02-17
summary: Kickoff for Sagecrest Medical onboarding to Redwood. Covered architecture choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO, KMS), initial pilot scope, success criteria, and immediate next steps to start a two-week pilot focusing on inpatient discharge summarization. Agreed to follow-up materials and weekly check-ins.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-14 15:00 PST | Duration 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Park, Priya Rao (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Dr. Amir Khan, Tasha Bell (Sagecrest)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving out time. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE owning this account. With me are Daniel our SE and Priya our CSM. How's everybody doing?
[00:06] Lena Ortiz: Good, thanks. Excited to get started.
[00:10] Dr. Amir Khan: Morning, afternoon, depends. Uh Amir here.
[00:13] Tasha Bell: Tasha, hi.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Quick agenda, we'll do intros, run through high-level onboarding plan, security and networking requirements, pilot scope and success metrics, and agree next steps.
[00:25] Daniel Park: Hi all, Daniel Park, I'm the SE who will help with the deployment, benchmarks and performance tuning. I'll be your point for VPC peering, dedicated capacity questions, and the inference test harness.
[00:35] Priya Rao: And I'm Priya, CSM, I'll be coordinating timelines and check-ins.
[00:40] Lena Ortiz: Cool. For context, our immediate need is a feature that summarizes inpatient discharge notes into a standardized summary for care coordination. We're pretty strict on PHI handling and auditability.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Great, that's helpful. Quick qualification: are you leaning hosted API first or do you need private deployment out of the gate?
[00:58] Dr. Amir Khan: We prefer private, ideally VPC with customer-managed keys, but we may be open to an initial hosted pilot if it reduces time to market. It depends on the data flow and whether tokens or raw notes leave our network.
[01:15] Daniel Park: Understood. Redwood supports a staged approach — hosted for quick POC, then Dedicated or Private (VPC / on-prem) for production with KMS integration. For PHI, typically customers run a pilot with pseudonymized data on hosted or use Dedicated with VPC egress controls.
[01:34] Lena Ortiz: What about audit logs and retention? We need full request/response logging for a period and access controls. SOC2 is non-negotiable.
[01:42] Maya Chen: We provide audit logs, role-based access, and we can tie into your SSO with SAML/SCIM. Redwood is SOC 2 compliant and we can share the report under NDA. We also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[01:58] Tasha Bell: Good. Also latency matters for some workflows; we need under 600ms median for the smaller note requests. Are you able to meet that?
[02:06] Daniel Park: On our hosted tier for smaller models we typically see sub-200ms for short prompts in our NYC region; Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency. For production SLOs, we recommend Dedicated pools or Private deployment pinned to specific GPU types. There is tradeoff with cost.
[02:25] Dr. Amir Khan: Cost is a factor. We have a procurement cycle, but we can commit to a POC budget. We mostly care about quality first then cost.
[02:33] Maya Chen: Totally — we can scope a two-week pilot that targets quality and perf. Daniel will run a benchmark with a sample of your notes and a set of prompts, measure latency and token cost so you can evaluate unit economics.
[02:44] Daniel Park: For the benchmark I'll need a representative dataset, ideally de-identified or PII-scrubbed. Also network contacts for VPC peering if you want private. We can provide a benchmark plan doc.
[02:55] Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a 500-note sample de-identified by Friday. Tasha will coordinate.
[03:00] Tasha Bell: Yep, I'll get that to you. Question on data residency — some of our facilities are in EU, we need EU hosting for those records. Can you confirm region choices?
[03:12] Daniel Park: Yes, we have multi-region options. For EU data we can run inference in EU regions or you can deploy Private in your VPC in EU cloud. We'll include region routing in the runbook.
[03:24] Priya Rao: I'll make a runbook that includes region selection, SSO steps, and contact points.
[03:30] Maya Chen: Security — just to clarify: you need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for keys, audit logs, and possibly AICPA confidentiality addendum?
[03:40] Lena Ortiz: Yeah, plus encryption in transit and at rest, and we want the ability to rotate keys. Also, who has access to debug logs? We need RBAC such that only certain roles can view transcriptions.
[03:52] Maya Chen: RBAC is standard — we can scope roles and ensure priors. Debug logs are access controlled. For key rotation, if you use customer-managed KMS we control rotation per your policy.
[04:04] Dr. Amir Khan: For the private option, what's the deployment model — appliance, VPC control plane, or packaged on-prem?
[04:11] Daniel Park: We offer a Private control plane with customer-managed networking, and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. On-prem requires a slightly longer lead time and validation; VPC-based Private is typically fastest for regulated workloads.
[04:24] Maya Chen: Timeline-wise, if we do hosted POC first, we can start bench tests within one week after you share the dataset. If you want Private, provisioning a Dedicated pool and VPC peering usually takes 2-4 weeks depending on networking.
[04:38] Tasha Bell: Sounds reasonable. Procurement wise we need pricing to show to finance. Can you send a pilot pricing estimate?
[04:46] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll send pilot pricing and examples of unit economics. We'll include token cost estimates and a Dedicated uplift option.
[04:54] Lena Ortiz: On integration, we want the output to be structured JSON and be able to call a function for downstream systems. Do you support function/tool calling?
[05:02] Daniel Park: Yes, we support structured output and tool-calling paradigms. We can return JSON schema validated outputs and integrate via webhooks or direct API.
[05:13] Dr. Amir Khan: Any concern with KV caching or long histories — our notes can be long, up to 2,500 tokens.
[05:20] Daniel Park: We support KV cache management and chunking strategies. For long documents we recommend prefix caching for common templates and dynamic chunking to keep tokens manageable. There might be some slight degradation on tail latency for very long contexts, which is why Dedicated can help.
[05:38] Tasha Bell: Who will be the technical contact for network setup?
[05:42] Maya Chen: Tasha, I think you mentioned network ops — can you share the contact?
[05:46] Tasha Bell: Yep, I'll share networkops@sagecrest.com, Ben K will be our network lead.
[05:50] Maya Chen: Great.
[05:52] Priya Rao: Next up pilot success metrics — what does success look like for Sagecrest after the two-week pilot?
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: Accuracy of summaries compared to clinician gold standard — target F1 ~0.85 on key fields, and median latency under 600ms for single note queries, and business acceptance by at least two care teams.
[06:12] Maya Chen: Good and measurable. We'll document those as acceptance criteria and include them in the pilot runbook.
[06:19] Daniel Park: On the technical side I'll instrument token counts, latency p50/p90, and error rates. We'll also include sample prompt variants to test regression.
[06:29] Dr. Amir Khan: One more security thing — do you support customer-supplied HSMs or only cloud KMS?
[06:35] Daniel Park: We support KMS integrations with customer-managed keys and in some enterprise cases HSM integration is possible via our Private deployment, we'll need to validate with security teams.
[06:46] Lena Ortiz: We'll need the SOC2 and pen test reports under NDA.
[06:50] Maya Chen: We'll send the SOC2 and pen test summary under NDA. I'll get legal to send an NDA link after this call.
[06:58] Tasha Bell: Any limitations on throughput during the pilot? We might have bursts when discharge cycles run.
[07:05] Daniel Park: For bursts we can provision temporary burst capacity on Dedicated; hosted has rate limits but we can often work with you for a pilot. We'll capture expected throughput in the runbook.
[07:17] Priya Rao: I'll set up weekly check-ins and a shared folder for artifacts, deck, runbook, benchmarks.
[07:24] Maya Chen: Let's recap action items and owners...
[07:28] Daniel Park: (interrupting) Quick note — sometimes transcription shows KV cache written as K-V cash in transcripts, sorry my pet peeve, but just a heads up for the runbook docs.
[07:36] (laughter)
[07:38] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Maya to share onboarding deck, pilot pricing, and SOC2 under NDA. 2) Daniel to share benchmark plan and begin test harness once dataset available. 3) Tasha to share de-identified 500-note sample and network lead contact. 4) Priya to schedule weekly syncs starting 2027-02-22.
[07:59] Lena Ortiz: That covers it. Will there be a kickoff workspace in Redwood console or do you share docs externally?
[08:06] Priya Rao: We'll share a Google Drive folder and also provision a project in the Redwood Console with initial roles for your team.
[08:15] Tasha Bell: Perfect. Any compliance questionnaire we need to fill?
[08:18] Maya Chen: We'll send a security questionnaire link and the SOC2.
[08:22] Dr. Amir Khan: Timeline note: procurement needs pricing by 2027-02-18 to hit our March deploy window.
[08:30] Maya Chen: We'll aim for that.
[08:33] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all.
[08:35] Maya Chen: Thanks, everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and set the first weekly meeting.
[08:40] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript: some speaker labels may be approximate; minor transcription errors present (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash, VPC sometimes typed as VPCe).
